summary: Bruno Galasek is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under the doctoral supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich (1862–1939) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Breslau, Munich, and Göttingen (Dr. phil. under Franz Kielhorn), habilitating at Breslau. He held posts at Heidelberg and Breslau, serving there as Ordentlicher Professor für Indologie (1921–1928).

Bruno Lindner (1853–1930) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig, Jena (under Carl Cappeller), and Tübingen (under Rudolf von Roth), also learning under Ernst Windisch, August Leskien, and Heinrich Hübschmann, and served as PD at Leipzig (1878–1919).

Bruno Lo Turco (born 1966) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at Sapienza University of Rome in 1997–1998, where he was a Ph.D. student (~1994–1998) and held a post around 2005.

Bruno Meissner (1868–1947) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the universities of Leipzig (~1885–1887) and Strasbourg (~1889–1892), and held posts at the University of Breslau (~1904–1920), Frederick William University Berlin (~1920–1936), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1920–1936).

Bruno Petzold (1873–1949) studied at Leipzig and Humboldt University, and later under Daito Shimaji, Shinsho Hanayama, and Hikoshiro Hoshino in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He taught at the First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.
Bruno Schindler (1882–1964) was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady (~1913–1919) and founded Asia Major in 1923. He later worked as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).

Bruno Snell (1896–1986) worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at the universities of Oxford (~1919–1920), Edinburgh, and Göttingen (~1920–1922), and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~1931–1961).

Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone, Martin Collcutt, Toru Funayama, and others, later serving as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017–2019).

Bryan J. Cuevas specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Emory and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Princeton and became John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State University.
Bryan W. Van Norden (born 1962) specializes in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991) and held the James Monroe Taylor Chair in Philosophy at Vassar College (~1997).

Bryce Ryan (1911–2005) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Washington and Harvard (M.A., Ph.D.). He held posts at Iowa State, Rutgers, the University of Ceylon, Cornell, Wayne State, and the University of Miami.

Buddhadeb Gorai is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed an M.A. at Jadavpur University (2006–2008). He became Assistant Professor at Deshbandhu College for Girls in 2014 and Founder and Editor-in-Chief of Bhāratāyana IKS Journal in 2026.

Buddhike Indrasena studied medicine and surgery across institutions including the University of Peradeniya, PGIM, and RCS England. Aside from Indology, he held surgical posts across Sri Lanka, a clinical fellowship in Singapore, and became Medical Statistician Associate at the World Academy of Medical Leadership.

Buddhodev Ghosh works in Indology and philosophy. He served in Project-Teaching Assistance at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (2022) and as a Project Associate at the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (2024–2025).

Bulcsu Siklós was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Charles R. Bawden and completed a PhD under Tadeusz Skorupski at the University of London. He held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

Bunga Fukui (1934–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda (~1978–2005).

Bunkyo Aoki (1886–1956) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University and under Kozui Otani (~1910–1917). In 1951, he succeeded Tokan Tada as a lecturer of Tibetan at the University of Tokyo.

Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) worked in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Japanology after studying at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda. He held posts at the Tokyo National Museum, the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, and served as Director of Nara National Museum (1975).

Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied at Otani University and Oxford under Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later serving in leadership roles at Otani University, lecturing at Tokyo University, and heading Nagoya Futsū Gakkō.
